elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall not pay Vendor any liquidated damages ... for any delay in providing a dependency"
"shall not pay Vendor any liquidated damages or penalties"

elements.element: Removal of the pre-agreed per-day sum (USD 25,000/day)
elements.evidence: amount struck: original "USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages" no longer appears

elements.element: Early-termination fee expressly capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: no early-termination fee or cap language in revised § 7.6

elements.element: Such fee is the sole liquidated amount payable
elements.evidence: no 'sole liquidated amount' or exclusivity wording present

reasons: The redline flips the operator and deletes the USD 25,000 per-day liquidated damages amount, so no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer under § 7.6 — the preferred position is met.

Fallback elements (early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount) are absent, but they are not required because the locked target is preferred and the levels are separate bargains.

Change is minimal: only the operator and the amount were altered; the trailing trigger phrase 'for any delay in providing a dependency' is retained from the original sentence, and no new exceptions, defined terms, or boilerplate were introduced.
Intent preserved: Vendor's dependency-delay concept remains addressed in the same sentence with no dangling mechanic or contradiction.
